questions.q: Which trait does the summary say allows you to compete even when you fear your rivals?
a: Courage
Composure
Consistency
Competitiveness
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes courage as the thing that enables you to be competitive in the first place.

questions.q: Why does the summary say running at 90% effort can make you faster?
a: The opposing muscles fight you less at that pace
Your body burns more fat at lower speeds
You avoid the temptation to sprint too early
Your stride becomes longer and more relaxed
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that at full effort the agonist and antagonist muscles struggle hardest against each other.

questions.q: What role does an antagonist muscle play while you run?
a: It pulls back and slows your movement
It pushes you forward with extra force
It stores energy for the final sprint
It relaxes so the joint can straighten
questions.why: Lesson 2 says agonists push you forward while antagonists pull back and slow you down.

questions.q: What three pillars does the summary say a good life should be built on?
a: Love, learning and labor
Health, wealth and wisdom
Focus, effort and reward
Purpose, passion and praise
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests judging yourself by whether your life is filled with love, learning and labor.

questions.q: Which of the three pillars does the summary say you have the most control over?
a: How much labor you put in
How much natural talent you have
How much luck comes your way
How much time you are given
questions.why: Lesson 3 says you cannot get more talent, luck or time, but you can always work more.
